title: 2022 - Whether Weather, Wind Speed and Temperature, Impacts Offensive Success in the NFL - Parks et al
file_name: 2022 - Whether Weather, Wind Speed and Temperature, Impacts Offensive Success in the NFL - Parks et al.pdf
universal_lens: Offensive efficiency is an additive expected-points functor over a filtered sample space of run/pass plays; weather enters as a static covariate, and summary statistics operate on the resulting EPA distribution, with graphical representations subject to scaling singularities.
gsi_mapping: Weather-aware play filtering defines a prior over offensive states; EPA likelihoods are conditioned on temperature and wind covariates, while conformal bands around per-play EPA capture epistemic uncertainty and out-of-distribution regimes such as missing weather or extreme events.
gse_mapping: Each run/pass play is a state transition parameterized by down, distance, and field position; temperature and wind covariates modify transition rewards through EPA, while pre-play filtering removes special-teams and penalty actions, yielding a Markov-like decision process for situational play selection.

primitives.name: Expected Points Added Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: EPA is calculated by taking the Expected Points at the beginning of the play and subtracting it from the Expected Points of the situation resulting from the play, hence the phrase Expected Points Added.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: EP: Expected Points, dimensionless; EPA: Expected Points Added, dimensionless; subscripts denote play state (begin/end).
primitives.assumptions: Expected Points depend only on down, distance, and field position; EPA is additive across plays; weather does not enter the EP model; run and pass are the only offensive actions under study.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Extreme EPA outliers such as long touchdowns or turnovers stretch box-plot whiskers and can obscure small mean differences between weather bins.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, EPA is the reward kernel of the Markov decision process whose states are (down, distance, field position) and whose actions are run/pass; in GSI, it is the log-likelihood surrogate for offensive efficiency conditioned on weather covariates.
layer2.telemetry: Per-play EPA distribution and mean EPA by play type and weather bin.

primitives.name: Weather State Encoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: ● nflfastR tracks 4 different weather conditions in 1 single column as shown below: ● The way nflfastR records this data makes it impossible to graph it without manipulation
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Weather record: a single concatenated string containing temperature, wind speed, and other conditions, dimensionless categorical; after parsing, T (temperature) and W (wind speed) are dimensionless covariates in the recorded units.
primitives.assumptions: nflfastR stores four weather fields in one concatenated column; the record is parseable into separate covariates; the pre-game weather snapshot is representative of the entire game.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Malformed or missing entries; no weather data before 2014; static snapshot fails if conditions change during the game; parsing ambiguities.

layer2.mapping: The raw nflfastR weather string is isomorphic to the product space of temperature, wind speed, and other conditions after parsing; in GSE it labels each transition, and in GSI it parameterizes the prior over game conditions.
layer2.telemetry: Fraction of plays with parseable weather; distribution of temperature and wind bins.

primitives.name: Offensive Play-Type Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: ○ All plays that were not runs and passes (takes out all special teams plays and plays resulting in penalties so we can just study runs and passes)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P: full set of plays, dimensionless index set; P_run/pass ⊆ P: retained run/pass plays, dimensionless; excluded plays are special-teams and penalty plays.
primitives.assumptions: Only runs and passes reflect offensive strategy; special-teams plays and plays resulting in penalties are irrelevant to the run/pass efficiency question; weather information is available for retained plays.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Selection bias if missing weather correlates with play type or venue; removal of penalties may discard informative offensive attempts; run/pass classification errors.

layer2.mapping: The filter is a projection kernel from the full play space to the offensive subspace of runs and passes; in GSE it defines the admissible action set, and in GSI it restricts the support of the EPA likelihood.
layer2.telemetry: Counts and proportions of run/pass versus excluded plays by weather condition.

primitives.name: Graphical Summary Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: However, due to box plots' property of extending out to capture all the extreme and irregular points, the plots don't do a great job of illustrating the seemingly small but actually impactful difference, which is why we display the means.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Box-plot quartiles and whiskers: dimensionless order statistics of EPA; mean EPA: dimensionless first moment of the per-bin EPA distribution.
primitives.assumptions: Box plots display median, quartiles, and extremes; means capture central tendency; a common scale is used across weather bins for comparability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Outliers extend whiskers and compress the visual scale, hiding small but impactful mean differences; choice of bin width affects perceived patterns.

layer2.mapping: The graphical summary is a lossy visualization kernel from the EPA distribution to box plots and means; in GSE it determines which reward differences are perceptible to decision makers, and in GSI it controls the empirical risk surface used for inference.
layer2.telemetry: Visual range of box plots; mean EPA values per weather bin; outlier count.

reasoning_traces.think:
The study treats each offensive play as a transition between game states, with reward measured by EPA as the Expected Points after the play minus the Expected Points before the play. Because Expected Points are a function of down, distance, and field position, EPA is an additive, state-conditioned reward that can be aggregated by play type and weather bin. The first primitive is therefore the EPA operator itself: a derived kernel that maps every run/pass transition to a real-valued reward. The second primitive is the weather-state encoder, an isomorphism that parses nflfastR’s single-column weather record into temperature and wind covariates; it is valid only under the assumption that the pre-game snapshot is representative of the whole game. The third primitive is the play-type filter, a projection kernel that removes special-teams and penalty plays so that the remaining sample reflects offensive choices. The fourth primitive is the graphical summary operator, which maps the EPA distribution to box plots and means; it highlights the breakdown regime where outliers stretch the plot and obscure small but meaningful mean differences. Together, these operators form a pipeline: filter, encode weather, compute EPA, summarize. The duality is between the raw event space of all plays and the analytic space of run/pass EPA conditional on weather. Failure modes include missing weather data before 2014, static-weather mismeasurement, selection bias from excluding penalties, and visual scaling that can hide or exaggerate effects. The operators are not independent: the filter changes the support of the EPA distribution, the encoder assigns covariates, and the summary operator determines which differences are visible to a decision maker.
